Brainternet

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The future of human integrated technology is here - In a world exclusive Carte Blanche shows local wits students together with singularity university use a brain to communicate with the internet.

Unique Selling Point:
Now in a world first and Carte Blanche exclusive we’ll show how Adam Pantanowitz and team have taken this one step further – in a soon to published paper that has been submitted to a journal, they can show a brain transmitting information between two computers. This is called the brain network - The footage is exclusive! This project uses two computers which were disconnected (no network connection, no wifi, no cables), the students encoded into flashing light information like the word hello/goodby (flashing light is similar to morse code and the signal is picked up by the cortex in the back of the brain), that word was then transmitted via the flashing light through the eye by looking at the light, to the back of the brain, called the visual cortex, now the technique is not new, but the transmission of the word from computer 1 to computer 2 through the human brain is a world first and entirely unique. It effectively turned the human brain into a non-cognitive passive network, and we were able to connect the two distinct computers without using traditional means, passing on information.

Brainternet works by converting electroencephalogram (EEG) signals (brain waves) in an open source brain live stream. A person wears a powered, mobile, internet accessible Emotiv EEG device for an extended period. During this time, the Emotiv transmits the EEG signals to a Raspberry Pi – a credit card sized little computer - live streams the signals to an application programming interface (code that allows software programmes to communicate), and displays data on a website that acts as a portal. This is currently an open website where the public can observe the individual’s brain activity.
Brainternet seeks to simplify a person’s understanding of their own brain and the brains of others. It does this through continuous monitoring of brain activity as well as enabling some interactivity. Brainternet can be further improved to classify recordings through a smart phone app that will provide data for a machine-learning algorithm. In future, there could be information transferred in both directions – inputs and outputs to the brain. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3-jRdZEA_Y
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LSdN--axYbA
Brainternet makes the uploading of your brain similar to an iot.


Summary:
By the 2030s we will be able to connect our brains to the internet via nanobots that will “provide full-immersion virtual reality from within the nervous system, provide direct brain-to-brain communication over the internet, and otherwise greatly expand human intelligence.”
What is consciousness? We might be one step closer to understanding the brain and therefore understanding our conscious minds. Two years ago, Prof. Adam Pantanowitz and two 4th year students at Wits were able to start bridging the gap between having our brains communicate with computers. They were able to …explain
The "Brainternet" project streams brainwaves onto the internet. Essentially, it turns the brain into an Internet of Things (IoT) node on the World Wide Web. IoT refers to connecting any device with an on and off switch to the internet. This technology has Global applications – medical diagnostics with epilepsy, hospitals had to induce seizures, but now they can diagnose remotely with a wearable device and live stream to early warn a patient, and even intervene at their location. Social applications – to be able to communicate remotely – we have been working through smartphones but we not it would just be wirelessly connected to your brain through an implant.

Further information:
Brain-machine interface technology/ Emerging neurotechnology
Negatives verse positives: - we will explore this during the program - we don't want to scare people. Basically the technology is neutral, but it's the user who will use it for bad or good. This is about education and teaching people who to use it positively and advance our civilization. Also, those who do not get used to the rapidly advancing technology will be left behind, and soon it wont be just the poor verse rich scale, but the tech verse non-tech people, with the former having great advantages is an technologically advanced world.
We are currently seeing the rise of “consciousness hackers” using techniques like non-invasive brain stimulation through EEG, nutrition, virtual reality, and ecstatic experiences to create environments for heightened consciousness and self-awareness - explore the trillion-dollar altered-states economy and how innovators and thought leaders are “harnessing rare and controversial states of consciousness to solve critical challenges and outperform the competition.” Keitumetsi the security expert will speak about this - and about the future of the iot and how we need to start thinking about protecting ourselves.
We’ve already connected two brains via the internet, allowing the two to communicate, and future-focused startups are researching the possibilities too. With an eye toward advanced brain-machine interfaces, last year Elon Musk unveiled Neuralink, a company whose ultimate goal is to merge the human mind with AI through a “neural lace.”
Many technologists predict we will one day merge with and, more speculatively, upload our minds onto machines – Uploading of consciousness.
Neuroscientist Kenneth Hayworth writes in Skeptic magazine, “All of today’s neuroscience models are fundamentally computational by nature, supporting the theoretical possibility of mind-uploading.” This might include connecting with other minds using digital networks or even uploading minds onto quantum computers, which can be in multiple states of computation at a given time.
What will the illusion of “I” feel like when our consciousness is directly plugged into the internet? Overall, what impact will the process of merging with technology have on the subjective experience of being human?
It is why many refer to their first altered-state experience as “waking up,” wherein they didn’t even realize they were asleep.

It would be great to speak to a futurist potentially if you know any?
MIT have a project
a team of biologists and security researchers have successfully infected a computer with a malicious program coded into a strand of DNA. https://techcrunch.com/2017/08/09/malicious-code-written-into-dna-infects-the-computer-that-reads-it/

Press Release:


Eskom Woes Continue
Eskom has been teetering on the edge of crisis for years and with the return of scheduled load-shedding, South Africans are fed-up. Without countless recovery plans and billions of rands poured into the power utility to keep it afloat, could the president’s new plan to unbundle Eskom provide the right solutions?
Producer: Mart-Marie Faure
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender
Researcher: Siniketiwe Hlanze
Watch the trailer


Script:


Imagine a future where our brains can speak to each other, feel what another person is feeling – even share experiences or thoughts. That is the future biomedical and electrical engineer and wits professor Adam Pantanowitz is trying to create.
Adam: “I love the ability to create something new from nothing.”
Enter Brainternet – cooked up in a wits university engineering lab in 2016. Pantanowitz who is also a professor at the well-known tech university, singularity, mentored two final year engineering students. Their task?... To convert brain waves into code a computer can understand.
Adam: “They ultimately we were the first ppl to have a livestream of brainwaves.”
Jemma Rogers was one of the Wits students.
Claire: “What can we interpret from those brainwaves?”
Jemma: “We can see if we raise our right hand, we can see the left hemisphere of our brain lighting up, so with something like epilepsy, we can see specific spikes in specific quadrants of the brain.”
Pantanowitz: “It was a live stream, that effectively was portable, that allowed you to stream your brain waves in real time wherever you went.”
Rogers showed me Brainternet working in real time...
Jemma: “Now we can place the emotive on my head… (show computer screen) Our brain sends thoughts through very small voltages and that’s what we’re seeing here…”
Rogers showed me how it works.
Jemma: “Right now you can see where i raise my arm right over there, and you can see movements, as i move my head the signal becomes more noisy.”
Pantanowitz has been pushing his inventions to their limits since high school. As he was diagnosed with a medical condition that kept him at home, he wanted to use technology to reconnect. This lead to his latest project.
BRAIN CONNECT IS A WORLD FIRST – WHERE THE HUMAN BRAIN HAS BEEN USED AS PART OF A DATA COMMUNICATION CHANNEL – BASICALLY YOUR BRAIN CAN CONNECT TO DISCONNECTED COMPUTERS.
Michael Dukes and Rachil Daye - two fourth year engineering wits students achieved success with pantanowitz last year.
Rachil: “We transmitted information from one comp to another through a human brain.”
Daye is completing his studies overseas, but spoke to us via skype.
Daye: “The point was to see if we could get a simple message - a word like hello or apple through the channel. And we showed this is possible to do.”
Adam: “So what happens in, someone who is going to be in the middle of the network, wears this device on their head, which is called Encephalogram. What happens is that person looks at flashing light that is being driven by a computer, and that first computer is encoding info into light.”
That information in this case is a word - like apple which is sent from computer 1 to computer 2 through your brain.
Adam: “That info is sent into brain through eyes, and it detected by eeg device, the info that’s encoded is sent wirelessly into comp, comp 1 and 2 disconnected apart from this channel through the person’s brain and effectively it can transmit words.”
Just 3 weeks into the project, they sent the word hello through Daye’s brain! (pointing at video)
Rachil: “It’s a lovely moment, you have no idea before you get into it, whether it’s even possible, from there it was just building on that and getting better and better results.”
Pantanowitz and Dukes let me take the driver’s seat and test it out.
Claire: “is it going to hurt?”
Mike: “it’s not going to hurt.”
Claire: “Get ready to be amazed.”
Adam: “The flashing light is driven by this computer, the computer encodes a message and based on how the light is flashing, it propagates a signal into your eyes, and your brain does it’s thing and recognises that signal.”
Claire: “HAHA Hopefully!”
My brain is only receiving data which is encoded in the form of the flashing light, so I have no idea what the word is until it appears on the screen.
Michael: “Try not to think about anything else, try not to move around too much, because that can lead to other electrical signals in your brain and disrupt the reading of the signal.”
(Beep beep beep)
Michael: “What you’ll see on this screen is the received…”
Claire: “The received word?”
Michael: “Like APPLE..”
Claire’s reaction: “That’s incredible!!!!”
Adam: “There’s that phrase that modern technology, that’s visually done, is indistinguishable from magic.”
The team foresees this technology allowing us to interact with our environment through receiving a message via the flashing light.
Michael: “There’s potentially a lot of good applications for ppl with disabilities, because they don’t have the motor skills to go and press buttons, it may be easier to just receive a message via looking at a light.”
Futurist at Flux trends Dion Chang believes connecting our brains to technology is the future of human and tech integration.
Deon: “This is transhumanism, so it is kind of, when we reach the stage of are we being cyborgs, or of cyborgs becoming us? The big debate is are we going to be working for the machines, or are the machines going to be working for us?”
While some find the future of integration exciting, others are more reserved voicing concerns around privacy and data collection.
CLAIRE: “A HISTORIAN OF TECH, MELVIN KRANZBERG, FAMOUSLY SAID TECH IS NOT GOOD, NOR BAD, NOR IS IT NEUTRAL SO PERHAPS IT LIES BEHIND THE INTENTION OF THE END USER?”
Adam: “The idea that your brain could ultimately be a tool that could be hacked - that’s a very frightening thought. But we were able to then pull back from that, and hopefully create a future that we can all live in.”
Cyber expert and technology author, Nnamdi Oranye believes our regulations will need to expand.
Nnamdi: “I think what’s going to be important in that time frame, is whether there is an ethical framework to have human-tech integration in place.”
He says we need to solve African problems, with African solutions.
Nnamdi: “Think a grandma whose low on insulin and needs to get her medication, so it’s farms that information to the doctor or pharmacy, the medication is sent to her immediately without her having to call.”
Dion: “We’re reaching tipping point of saying, this kind of a lifestyle that we’ve learnt from the 20th century is not bringing us happiness, what is next? Seeding some of those responsibilities to machines or AI, might just be that answer.”
CLAIRE: “RIGHT NOW, PHONES, WATCHES AND LAPTOPS ARE EXTERNAL DEVICES BUT WITH TECHNOLOGY, THEY WILL SOON BE INTEGRATED WITH OUR BODIES.”
According to futurists by 2050, we may be able to cheat death and upload our consciousness onto the internet.
Adam: “Our brains, they have an ability to change, and should we introduce new info about computers to our brains, I think our brains are going to react to that on in a very natural way.”
But not everyone is ready to hook their brains up to the internet just yet.
Nnamdi: “I’m def not an early adopter, i think with time it’s a fascinating tech as a hobbyist, but to have my brain plugged in, just yet… no.” 8:03

Adam: “Our brains, they have an ability to change, and should we introduce new info about computers to our brains, I think our brains are going to react to that on in a very natural way.” But not everyone is ready to hook their brains up to the internet just yet. Nnamdi: “I’m def not an early adopter, i think with time it’s a fascinating tech as a hobbyist, but to have my brain plugged in, just yet… no.” 8:03

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The future of human integrated technology is here - In a world exclusive Carte Blanche shows local wits students together with singularity university use a brain to communicate with the internet.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Now in a world first and Carte Blanche exclusive we’ll show how Adam Pantanowitz and team have taken this one step further – in a soon to published paper that has been submitted to a journal, they can show a brain transmitting information between two computers. This is called the brain network - The footage is exclusive! This project uses two computers which were disconnected (no network connection, no wifi, no cables), the students encoded into flashing light information like the word hello/goodby (flashing light is similar to morse code and the signal is picked up by the cortex in the back of the brain), that word was then transmitted via the flashing light through the eye by looking at the light, to the back of the brain, called the visual cortex, now the technique is not new, but the transmission of the word from computer 1 to computer 2 through the human brain is a world first and entirely unique. It effectively turned the human brain into a non-cognitive passive network, and we were able to connect the two distinct computers without using traditional means, passing on information. Brainternet works by converting electroencephalogram (EEG) signals (brain waves) in an open source brain live stream. A person wears a powered, mobile, internet accessible Emotiv EEG device for an extended period. During this time, the Emotiv transmits the EEG signals to a Raspberry Pi – a credit card sized little computer - live streams the signals to an application programming interface (code that allows software programmes to communicate), and displays data on a website that acts as a portal. This is currently an open website where the public can observe the individual’s brain activity. Brainternet seeks to simplify a person’s understanding of their own brain and the brains of others. It does this through continuous monitoring of brain activity as well as enabling some interactivity. Brainternet can be further improved to classify recordings through a smart phone app that will provide data for a machine-learning algorithm. In future, there could be information transferred in both directions – inputs and outputs to the brain. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3-jRdZEA_Y https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LSdN--axYbA Brainternet makes the uploading of your brain similar to an iot.
metadata.Summary: By the 2030s we will be able to connect our brains to the internet via nanobots that will “provide full-immersion virtual reality from within the nervous system, provide direct brain-to-brain communication over the internet, and otherwise greatly expand human intelligence.” What is consciousness? We might be one step closer to understanding the brain and therefore understanding our conscious minds. Two years ago, Prof. Adam Pantanowitz and two 4th year students at Wits were able to start bridging the gap between having our brains communicate with computers. They were able to …explain The "Brainternet" project streams brainwaves onto the internet. Essentially, it turns the brain into an Internet of Things (IoT) node on the World Wide Web. IoT refers to connecting any device with an on and off switch to the internet. This technology has Global applications – medical diagnostics with epilepsy, hospitals had to induce seizures, but now they can diagnose remotely with a wearable device and live stream to early warn a patient, and even intervene at their location. Social applications – to be able to communicate remotely – we have been working through smartphones but we not it would just be wirelessly connected to your brain through an implant.
metadata.Further information: Brain-machine interface technology/ Emerging neurotechnology Negatives verse positives: - we will explore this during the program - we don't want to scare people. Basically the technology is neutral, but it's the user who will use it for bad or good. This is about education and teaching people who to use it positively and advance our civilization. Also, those who do not get used to the rapidly advancing technology will be left behind, and soon it wont be just the poor verse rich scale, but the tech verse non-tech people, with the former having great advantages is an technologically advanced world. We are currently seeing the rise of “consciousness hackers” using techniques like non-invasive brain stimulation through EEG, nutrition, virtual reality, and ecstatic experiences to create environments for heightened consciousness and self-awareness - explore the trillion-dollar altered-states economy and how innovators and thought leaders are “harnessing rare and controversial states of consciousness to solve critical challenges and outperform the competition.” Keitumetsi the security expert will speak about this - and about the future of the iot and how we need to start thinking about protecting ourselves. We’ve already connected two brains via the internet, allowing the two to communicate, and future-focused startups are researching the possibilities too. With an eye toward advanced brain-machine interfaces, last year Elon Musk unveiled Neuralink, a company whose ultimate goal is to merge the human mind with AI through a “neural lace.” Many technologists predict we will one day merge with and, more speculatively, upload our minds onto machines – Uploading of consciousness. Neuroscientist Kenneth Hayworth writes in Skeptic magazine, “All of today’s neuroscience models are fundamentally computational by nature, supporting the theoretical possibility of mind-uploading.” This might include connecting with other minds using digital networks or even uploading minds onto quantum computers, which can be in multiple states of computation at a given time. What will the illusion of “I” feel like when our consciousness is directly plugged into the internet? Overall, what impact will the process of merging with technology have on the subjective experience of being human? It is why many refer to their first altered-state experience as “waking up,” wherein they didn’t even realize they were asleep. It would be great to speak to a futurist potentially if you know any?
